title: CSIRO Uses Serverless Architecture to Query 100x More Genomic Variants on AWS
gist: CSIRO's Serverless Beacon (sBeacon) implements the GA4GH Beacon standard on AWS S3, Lambda, Athena and DynamoDB. It leaves compressed VCF files in S3 and reads only the needed genomic regions through HTTP byte-range requests, instead of loading data into a central database. On 1000 Genomes chromosome 1 (2,504 samples, 1.1 GB), onboarding took 18 seconds and a 10,000 base-pair query averaged 1.52 seconds at about USD 0.00013 in compute.

insights.claim: CSIRO built Serverless Beacon (sBeacon), which queries genomic variant data without copying large datasets into a central database. It uses Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, Amazon Athena and Amazon DynamoDB to implement the GA4GH Beacon standard while the underlying data stays in its original storage.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: This is a reference case for AWS serverless in scientific and healthcare data workloads that would otherwise need dedicated databases.

insights.claim: sBeacon separates genomic data from search metadata: Variant Call Format (VCF) files stay in Amazon S3, while metadata such as disease status, age and location is indexed separately in Athena tables created at onboarding, and CSIRO's Ontoserver handles ontology terms so queries can combine genomic and phenotypic information.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Splitting small metadata indexes from bulk object storage is a reusable pattern for cutting the cost of querying large scientific datasets.

insights.claim: In sBeacon, API Gateway routes variant queries to Lambda functions that identify the relevant datasets and genomic regions. The Variant Querying Module then uses bcftools and htslib to fetch only the needed portions of VCF files through HTTP byte-range requests, without transferring whole files.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Byte-range reads keep data transfer and compute costs proportional to the query rather than the dataset size.

insights.claim: CSIRO's Anuradha Wickramarachchi said a key sBeacon design choice was keeping genomic data in its most compressed form and querying it while still compressed.
insights.speaker: Anuradha Wickramarachchi
insights.so_what: Querying compressed data in place reduces storage and egress costs for genomics at scale.

insights.claim: CSIRO benchmarked sBeacon on chromosome 1 from the 1000 Genomes Project (2,504 samples in a 1.1 GB compressed VCF): onboarding took 18 seconds, and a query covering 10,000 base pairs averaged 1.52 seconds at an estimated compute cost of USD 0.00013.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Fractions of a cent per query make large-cohort genomic search economically trivial, which favours broader data sharing.
insights.locator: CSIRO evaluated the architecture using chromosome 1

insights.claim: sBeacon query latency stayed broadly consistent as the number of matching variants rose from four to 400.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Latency that is insensitive to result size suggests the serverless fan-out scales well for interactive genomic queries.
insights.locator: CSIRO evaluated the architecture using chromosome 1

insights.claim: Earlier sBeacon research published in Nature Biotechnology reported support for up to 40 million individuals and 3 billion genomic locations.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: The architecture is designed for population-scale genomics programmes, not just research cohorts.
insights.locator: The design builds on earlier sBeacon research

insights.claim: The GA4GH Beacon protocol uses a federated model that lets organizations keep control of their genomic data while exposing standardized query interfaces, without prescribing a storage technology. CSIRO's 2026 sBeacon implementation adds elastic cloud query execution while the genomic files stay in object storage.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Federated query-in-place fits data-sovereignty requirements in health data and could widen cloud adoption in regulated genomics.
insights.locator: The design builds on earlier sBeacon research
